title: Healthcare Security Seller Cheatsheet — Audit & Data Handling Claims
body:
Purpose:
This is a concise seller-facing cheatsheet for Healthcare/Payor deals. Objective: give AEs, CSEs and solutions engineers plain-language claim snippets, competitor talking points, and an audit-log + data handling checklist they can drop into RFPs, security reviews, and contract redlines.

Audience:
- AE/CSE during early security screening calls
- Solutions Engineers prepping security review decks
- Legal and Sales when drafting BAAs and audit language

Top-line positioning (one-liners):
- "Redwood Inference runs inference without absorbing customer content: there is no training-on-customer-data, and all customer request/response telemetry is segregated and auditable."
- "We support SOC 2 Type II controls, ISO-ready documentation, and HIPAA via an executed BAA — with configurable data residency and encryption at rest and in transit."

Quick objection scripts (engineering/security buyer):
- Buyer: "How do you prevent PHI leakage into models?"
  - Seller: "We don't use customer request/response data for model training. For private deployments customers can run the full control plane in their VPC or on-prem and keep all tokens off our hosted paths. Additionally, prefix/KV caches are tenant-isolated and never shared across customers."
- Buyer: "What about third-party dependencies?"
  - Seller: "We have an approved component inventory, and our supply chain assessments are part of SOC2 and ISO artifact sets. For high-risk customers we can provide SBOM extracts and dependency reports during the security review."

Suggested audit-log language (boilerplate to drop into security evidence):
- "Redwood maintains immutable audit logs for all admin and platform-level activities. Request/response traces for inference calls are captured with per-request IDs, timestamps, model&version metadata, route, and anonymized cost metrics. Access to audit logs is role-gated and exported on demand to customer-managed sinks (S3/GCS) for retention and e-discovery."
- "Retention: default 90 days for request/response traces on hosted plans; Dedicated/Private deployments can configure retention policies up to 'customer-defined' durations and export via TLS-encrypted streams to the customer's logging endpoints."

SOC2/ISO mapping (seller notes — do not publish externally without legal signoff):
- Logical access: RBAC for console/API, MFA enforced for all prod accounts, least-privilege service principals. Evidence: IAM policies, access review artifacts, MFA enforcement logs.
- Change management: PR-based code deploys, CI/CD audit trail, staged rollouts with canary gates. Evidence: Git commit history, CI build logs, rollback runbooks.
- Incident response: IR runbook, playbooks, tabletop exercises, SLA for incident notifications to customers. Evidence: tabletop notes, postmortems.
- Data encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AEAD encryption at rest using customer-managed KMS for Private; hosted uses HSM-backed KMS. Evidence: TLS configurations, KMS key policies.

HIPAA-specific checklist for sellers (talking points + evidence to gather):
- BAA: We sign BAAs with customers needing HIPAA coverage. Template BAA exists; legal should be looped for redlines.
- PHI handling: Clearly document which API endpoints will carry PHI and propose either Private deployment or Dedicated isolation with explicit network controls.
- Access controls: Ensure minimal staff with access to PHI; document admin access exceptions and approval flow.
- Audit logs: Provide sample log schema + export to customer SOC.
- Business continuity: Backup retention and restore SLAs; encrypted backups.
- Recommended customer ask: "Can you demonstrate a test export of inference logs into our secure S3 bucket?" — this is our standard demo step.

Competitive notes (short bullets — useful to justify Redwood strengths):
- Anthropic/OpenAI: Strong baseline security but "training on customer data" ambiguity is a recurring buyer question. Position Redwood as explicit: no training on customer live-proxy data + private deployment option.
- Cloud vendors (AWS/Azure): Provide endpoint hosting but lack a unified inference runtime optimised for LLM economics and token-level observability. Angle: Redwood adds transparency (token/cost/latency breakdowns) and inference-specialized fallbacks.
- Inference-only vendors: Good on performance but often weaker on developer UX and rollout tooling (A/B, canary). Redwood: emphasize rollouts, model pinning, and automatic fallback policies.

Proof-points & artifacts to have ready (pre-flight checklist for AE/CSE):
- SOC2 Type II report PDF (redacted) or summary one-pager.
- ISO scope document + lead auditor contact (if customer requests).
- BAA template and a short FAQ on common redlines we accept/reject.
- Audit-log sample (synthetic) showing request id, timestamp, model, route, anonymized cost, and retention header.
- Short demo script: show live export of logs to a pre-provisioned S3 (10–15 minutes).

Customer-facing claim snippets (for proposals/RFPs):
- "Redwood Inference offers SOC2 Type II controls and ISO-aligned documentation for our production inference platform. We will enter into a BAA for HIPAA-covered workloads and provide exportable, immutable audit logs for all inference activity. For customers requiring private control, Redwood supports VPC and on-prem deployments with customer-managed KMS."

Redlines we commonly accept (legal-friendly bullets):
- Reasonable encryption-at-rest and in-transit clauses (we provide TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest by default).
- Audit log exports on customer request (with a mutual NDAs for sensitive logs if necessary).

Redlines we push back on / escalate to Legal:
- Language implying continuous training or model updates using customer data (we reject).
- Unlimited log retention obligations on the hosted API without additional pricing (we can support for Dedicated/Private).

Demo checklist for security review call (SE-run):
1) Prepare SOC2 one-pager and BAA draft in advance.
2) Build a synthetic workload with PHI-like fields (anonymized) to demonstrate export pipeline.
3) Show token/cost/latency dashboard for a short workload and highlight per-request trace.
4) Walk through RBAC roles and show a live role-change audit entry.
5) Execute a mock export to the customer's S3/GCS (or show logs already exported).

Open items / TODOs (internal):
- Create sanitized 'audit-log sample' artifact (PR assigned to ENG-obs).
- Legal: finalize BAA template for healthcare vertical (Jira: GTM-1145).
- Product: prepare a short SOC2 FAQ (1-pager) for AEs (owner: Lena).

Notes to sellers (voice & tone):
- Keep it concrete and operational: buyers care about steps, not philosophical promises.
- Avoid "we never" absolutes without legal signoff — prefer "we do not use customer request/response data for model training" and reference config options (Private/Dedicated).
- When in doubt, escalate to Solutions Engineering for a live technical walkthrough.

Appendix: short sample snippet for RFP (one paragraph):
- "Redwood Inference maintains industry-standard security controls: SOC2 Type II, ISO-aligned artifacts, and a BAA for HIPAA-covered processing. Customers can choose hosted, Dedicated (isolated capacity), or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment modes. Audit logs containing per-request metadata are available for export; encryption is enforced in transit and at rest, and keys can be managed by the customer for Private deployments."

End of cheatsheet.

Document history: informal working draft — do not circulate externally until Legal signs off on BAA and SOC2 redactions.
